item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":15,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Mexico inherited strong macroeconomic institutions and a record of prudent monetary and fiscal policy, including an autonomous central bank, inflation targeting, fiscal consolidation, improved debt management, and strengthened macroprudential regulation. Earlier structural reforms also produced measurable gains in tax revenue, financial access, telecommunications, competition, and subnational debt management, although implementation gaps remained in labor, education quality, anticorruption, judicial, innovation, fiscal federalism, health, and social-benefit reforms.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Primarily inherited pre-2023 baseline; useful context for evaluating AMLO's 2023 choices, not evidence of AMLO-specific implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The document describes successive Mexican governments and reforms before AMLO's 2023 period; attribution to AMLO is not established.","limitations":["The diagnostic predates AMLO's 2023 period and does not identify which inherited policies AMLO retained, changed, or reversed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":20,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"Mexico faced substantial exposure to natural hazards, regional inequality, weak convergence, low productivity, informality, and inadequate infrastructure investment. By 2017, growth had averaged about 2.4 percent since 1980; public infrastructure investment averaged 3.2 percent of GDP in 2008–15 and fell to 2.6 percent in 2017; regional GDP per capita and productivity gaps were pronounced; and informal employment remained about 56.5–56.9 percent.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Inherited baseline relevant to 2023; the cited indicators largely end in 2017 or earlier.","ruler_attribution":"The document attributes these conditions to long-run structural factors and successive governments, not specifically to AMLO.","limitations":["No 2023 outcome data or AMLO policy attribution is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":25,"end_unit":32,"fact_summary":"Mexico achieved moderate reductions in monetary and multidimensional poverty and expanded targeted social protection and health coverage, but poverty remained high, shared prosperity lagged regional peers, and severe territorial, indigenous, rural, gender, education, financial-access, rule-of-law, corruption, crime, and service-delivery inequalities persisted. The report identifies weak enforcement, impunity, fragmented programs, rigid spending, limited coordination, and unequal transfers as major constraints.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.10","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.7","6B.8","6B.10","7B.7","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Inherited pre-2023 baseline, with some indicators through 2017.","ruler_attribution":"The diagnostic evaluates national and subnational systems over preceding decades and does not establish AMLO-specific responsibility.","limitations":["The source provides national conditions and policy-system analysis rather than a 2023 ruler-period evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":29,"end_unit":35,"fact_summary":"Mexico had developed disaster-risk and climate institutions, including FONDEN, a climate law, a national climate strategy, a special climate program, NDCs, a climate fund, and carbon-pricing instruments. Conservation payments reduced forest-cover loss and had small poverty effects, but water stress, underinvestment, environmental degradation, climate vulnerability, and weak implementation capacity remained substantial.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.10","3B.9","3B.10","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Inherited institutional baseline; evidence is mainly through 2018 and does not cover AMLO's 2023 decisions.","ruler_attribution":"The document attributes institutions and policies to the Mexican state and prior governments, not specifically to AMLO.","limitations":["No evidence is supplied about whether AMLO preserved, weakened, funded, or replaced these institutions in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":31,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"Mexico's rule-of-law and accountability environment was weak: it ranked poorly on rule-of-law, criminal-justice, corruption, and impunity measures; reported crime resolution probability was very low; and public-resource diversion rarely resulted in convictions. The diagnostic nevertheless records reforms to oral commercial justice, transparency, and the National Anticorruption System, while noting incomplete implementation and risks of institutional recapture.","question_ids":["2B.6","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.10","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","5B.5","5B.7","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Inherited baseline, primarily 2015–2018.","ruler_attribution":"The source discusses national institutions and prior reforms without attributing the documented failures or reforms specifically to AMLO.","limitations":["No AMLO-era institutional actions, appointments, court responses, or 2023 accountability outcomes are provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":43,"end_unit":46,"fact_summary":"Mexican authorities previously responded to the 2014 oil-price shock with additional tax revenue, expenditure rationalization, and fiscal consolidation; public debt stabilized and later declined while growth continued. However, fiscal space and public investment were constrained, with public investment falling substantially by 2017 and long-term pressures from pensions, health, aging, and rigid spending remaining.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Pre-2023 inherited fiscal baseline.","ruler_attribution":"The report refers to Mexican authorities collectively and does not identify AMLO as responsible.","limitations":["The document does not show AMLO's 2023 fiscal decisions or their effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":57,"end_unit":64,"fact_summary":"Before 2023, education access was near universal in primary and lower secondary schooling, but upper-secondary enrollment and completion were low, learning outcomes lagged OECD averages, and indigenous, rural, gender, and regional gaps were large. Early-childhood staffing ratios were unfavorable, and only about half of 15-year-olds achieved skills considered necessary for effective participation in society and work.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.8","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Inherited baseline using data mostly through 2017.","ruler_attribution":"No AMLO-specific education decisions or outcomes are identified.","limitations":["The evidence does not establish whether AMLO's 2023 education policies improved or worsened these conditions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":73,"end_unit":77,"fact_summary":"Health coverage expanded substantially before 2023: the share without access to health care fell from 38.4 percent in 2008 to 15.5 percent in 2016, and Seguro Popular covered tens of millions. Nevertheless, health spending remained low, out-of-pocket costs high, the system fragmented, resources inefficiently allocated, and regional and income disparities in staffing, quality, and outcomes persisted.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.10","5B.6","5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Inherited baseline, mainly 2014–2016.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes prior Mexican health reforms and system conditions, not AMLO's 2023 administration.","limitations":["No evidence is supplied on AMLO's health-system restructuring or 2023 service outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":87,"end_unit":90,"fact_summary":"Mexico had established climate-governance and disaster-finance instruments, including FONDEN, catastrophe insurance, a risk atlas, climate legislation, an NDC, a climate fund, and a carbon tax. The framework was described as comprehensive but evolving; feasibility analysis, emissions-trading implementation, low carbon-tax incentives, coordination, and adaptation remained unresolved challenges.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.10","3B.9","3B.10","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Inherited framework documented through approximately 2018.","ruler_attribution":"The document does not attribute the framework's strengths or shortcomings specifically to AMLO.","limitations":["No 2023 evidence is supplied on climate implementation, disaster response, or institutional continuity."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":95,"end_unit":103,"fact_summary":"The 2012–2017 reform package had mixed implementation: tax, financial, telecommunications, election, competition, and energy reforms were relatively advanced, while labor, education quality, anticorruption, judicial, innovation, and fiscal-federalism reforms had gaps; agricultural, health, unemployment-insurance, pension, and social-benefit reforms showed insufficient progress. Reported results included increased tax revenue, financial access, mobile broadband, and reduced telecommunications prices, but the overall growth effect had not met expectations and implementation lagged.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.2","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Pre-AMLO inherited policy baseline; results mainly through 2017.","ruler_attribution":"The reforms are attributed to the Pacto por México and governments before AMLO; the source does not assess AMLO.","limitations":["The document cannot establish AMLO's program, appointments, mobilization, implementation, adaptation, or 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":104,"end_unit":108,"fact_summary":"Mexico's justice and security systems faced arbitrary arrests, forced confessions, falsified evidence, wrongful convictions, unlawful detention, police and prison abuses, unequal access to justice, lengthy pretrial detention, widespread corruption, low crime-resolution rates, rising homicides, extortion, organized crime, and severe gender-based violence. The source identifies institutional reform, accountability, social prevention, youth support, and effective criminal-justice implementation as necessary responses.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.6","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","5B.5","5B.7","6B.3","6B.6","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Inherited baseline, with crime figures through 2017 and institutional evidence through 2018.","ruler_attribution":"The source discusses national and prior administrations' systems; it does not assign these outcomes to AMLO.","limitations":["No 2023 violence, security-policy, oversight, remedy, or correction evidence is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":109,"end_unit":115,"fact_summary":"Mexico's social-protection, health, fiscal-transfer, and investment systems were fragmented and unequal. There were thousands of social programs with overlapping beneficiaries; health insurance was divided by employment status; subnational spending and service access varied sharply; discretionary transfers reduced transparency; and weak coordination and long-term planning produced poorly located housing, infrastructure gaps, and suboptimal public-private investment.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.7","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Inherited baseline, mainly 2006–2018.","ruler_attribution":"The diagnostic describes institutional structures and prior reforms without specific AMLO attribution.","limitations":["No evidence is supplied on whether AMLO consolidated programs, changed transfers, improved coordination, or altered implementation in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-68ba67316f9e3122","start_unit":15,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"Mexico's democratic system had become more electorally competitive and redistributed power among parties and states, but local observers also reported persistent or expanded rent-seeking and weak accountability. The 2018 election produced a landslide victory for MORENA, but this source does not describe the resulting administration's conduct.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.5","4B.8","4B.10","7B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Context immediately preceding AMLO's presidency; the cited discussion ends with the 2018 election.","ruler_attribution":"AMLO is mentioned only indirectly through MORENA's 2018 electoral victory; no 2023 conduct is documented.","limitations":["The source does not provide evidence about AMLO's 2023 democratic, integrity, or effectiveness record."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied source is a 2018 World Bank diagnostic containing mostly inherited national conditions and prior reforms; it provides little direct evidence about Andrés Manuel López Obrador's actions or outcomes in 2023.","No supplied evidence concerns nuclear weapons, arms control, proliferation, or other existential-risk governance specifically attributable to AMLO; the climate and disaster-risk facts are the closest relevant dual-use or catastrophic-risk material."]}
